Solution written to **`/home/kara/go-cli-static-format-gate.md`** (495 lines, self-contained).

## What I did

The working directory had no repo, so I reconstructed the failure mode in a scratch module, then implemented and empirically verified the fix.

**Root cause:** "gofmt-clean" has no executable definition in a typical Go repo. `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test` are all indifferent to formatting, so rot accumulates behind green checks.

**Fix:** one in-repo package `internal/fmtcheck` is the single check-only definition; three surfaces invoke it with the byte-identical command:
- `TestGofmt` (no `testing.Short()` skip) → caught by plain `go test ./...`
- Makefile target → `go test -count=1 -run TestGofmt ./internal/fmtcheck`
- CI step → same exact string, verified identical with `diff`

## Verified against Go 1.26.0

| Claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline build/vet/test green with `gofmt` rot | ✅ reproduced |
| Gate catches rot, `testdata/` skipped | ✅ reports only `cmd/app/main.go` |
| `go test -short ./...` still enforces | ✅ fails on rot |
| Root located via `go.mod` walk-up, not cwd | ✅ test runs in `internal/fmtcheck`, still finds `cmd/app` |
| Parse errors not double-reported | ✅ gate passes, `go build` reports the syntax error |
| `format.Source` ≡ `gofmt` binary | ✅ **5,597 files, 0 divergences** (Go stdlib) |
| Unsorted imports / legacy `// +build` / trailing WS / misaligned comments | ✅ all flagged by both |
| Makefile vs CI command | ✅ byte-identical |

The document includes full copy-pasteable source, the Makefile/CI snippets, a regression test (`TestCheckSemantics`) locking in the two non-obvious rules, the differential harness source, and adaptation steps for an existing module (only change needed: the module path in the test import).

signatures.description: Go repo where gofmt is not gated: build/vet/test all green while formatting rot accumulates. Fix proven at coding-hermes/boardctl BT-028 (commit 5ff8e2e): create a tiny in-repo package (internal/fmtcheck) that is the SINGLE check-only definition of gofmt-clean, then have three surfaces invoke that one checker so they cannot drift: a Makefile target (go test -count=1 -run TestGofmt ./internal/fmtcheck), a CI step with the byte-identical command, and the test itself picked up by plain `go test ./...` with NO testing.Short() skip so a -short CI test step still enforces it. Two non-obvious findings worth caching: (1) in Go 1.26 go/format.Source output is byte-identical to the gofmt binary on real code - a differential harness over 39 repo files found 0 divergences and probes for unsorted imports, legacy // +build-only tags, trailing whitespace and misaligned field comments were ALL flagged, so an in-process checker is a legitimate substitute for `gofmt -l` and needs no external binary; (2) format.Source returns an error on unparseable files, so treat a parse error as NOT-a-formatting-finding and leave it to build/vet, otherwise the gate double-reports compile errors. Also skip directories named testdata (fixtures may hold intentionally unformatted snippets) and locate the repo root by walking up to go.mod instead of trusting the cwd.
